claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a child - my son Alex, he's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a son, Alex, who is 11 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex a bit better.

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or equivalent support like food, clothes, or pocket money) towards looking after him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help out with things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about your contributions.

Approximately how much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month? And do you know what the current Child Benefit rate is, or are you contributing an amount that would be at least equal to or more than the Child Benefit payment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £30 a week towards his upkeep - buying him clothes, school dinner money, things he needs, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

How long has Alex been living away from you? Is it more than 8 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's been living with his mum for quite a while now - it's definitely been more than a couple of months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

One more important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as his mum or another person he lives with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him - nobody who lives with him is claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16, so age-qualified)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you, but has been living away for more than 8 weeks
- You contribute approximately £30 per week towards his upkeep
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The key factor here is your contributions. According to the rules, if your child lives with someone else for more than 8 weeks, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.

Current Child Benefit rates are approximately £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child. Since you're contributing around £30 per week on clothes, school supplies, and other needs, this meets the contribution threshold.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet the eligibility requirements because:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing approximately £30 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the standard Child Benefit payment
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important notes:**
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so it's good that no one else is claiming for Alex
- You should keep records of your contributions in case HMRC needs to verify them
- If your income or your partner's income is over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. If your circumstances change (such as the amount you contribute or if someone else starts claiming), you should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office.
